title: You are the true Creator
hookLine: too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee: You are the true Creator, my Master (Asa M4, ang 11)
tomorrow: A pool of fire and water

lines: THE POTTER'S MARK ON THE BASE.
TONIGHT: READ THE MARK ON THE DAY.
cards: Pick up a handmade bowl at a craft fair and turn it over. On the bottom, pressed into the clay, there's often a little mark: initials, a symbol, the potter's stamp. The bowl doesn't know it's there.

It just holds soup. But the mark says someone shaped this, on purpose, with their hands. Guru Ram Das looks at a whole day that way: the light this morning, the people in it, the breath you're breathing now.
Tonight's shabad turns the day over and reads the mark.

teach.h: TOO KARTAA SACHIAAR: YOU ARE THE TRUE MAKER.
teach.b: The second So Purakh shabad, by Guru Ram Das, opens: too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee. You are the true Creator, my Master. Kartaa is the maker, the same word as in the Mool Mantar's karta purakh.
Sachiaar is true. And maiddaa saanee, my Master, is said in western Punjabi forms, the speech of the plains around Multan, so even the grammar sounds like someone talking at home.

teach.h: WHAT YOU GIVE IS WHAT I RECEIVE.
teach.b: Then, in paraphrase: whatever pleases You comes to pass; whatever You give, that is what I receive. All belongs to You, and all meditate on You. The one You bless receives the jewel of the Name.
The shabad gives the two directions a person can face: the gurmukh, turned toward the Guru, finds it; the manmukh, turned toward the self, loses it. Then come two pictures.
You Yourself separate us, the shabad says, and You Yourself bring us together.

teach.h: YOU ARE THE RIVER; ALL IS IN YOU.
teach.b: And: You are the river, and everything is within You; without You, there is no other. All beings are Your play. So the Maker isn't standing outside the day, like a potter who walked away from the wheel.

The Maker is the river the whole day flows in. For Sikhs saying Rehras, that changes what thank you means at dusk: not thanks sent off to a distant address, but the bowl noticing the hands still holding it.
And the closing note is trust, said simply: You are my Master.

how: Too kartaa sachiaar is the second shabad of the So Purakh group in Rehras Sahib, recited each evening; its line that the Lord is the river within which all things are is often quoted in Sikh teaching.

o: the Maker, the one who made all things
a servant who carries out a master's will
the one who keeps count of every deed

games.q: the true Creator — tap the pairs.
p: turned toward the Guru: finds it
turned toward the self: loses it

s: the shabad pictures the Maker as far away from creation
it says You are the river, and everything is within You.
maiddaa saanee uses western Punjabi forms
the speech of the plains around Multan; my Master.
the shabad says the Lord both separates and unites
You Yourself separate, and You Yourself bring together.

games.q: Guru Ram Das gives a picture of how the Maker relates to everything made. which is it?
o: a potter who has left the wheel.
the river, with everything within it.
a king far off in a palace.
games.why: You are the river, and everything is within You; without You there is no other.

practice: Turn today over, like the bowl, and find three things you didn't make yourself: the morning light, someone who cooked or drove or helped, the breath itself.
Give each one a quiet thank you; if you pray, you can use the shabad's own words, too kartaa sachiaar maiddaa saanee, or simply Waheguru. Then rest.

wordCard.voice: Kartaa, the Maker: Guru Ram Das calls the Lord the true Maker and his Master, the river in which everything flows.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: kartaa, the Maker; as in the Mool Mantar's karta purakh.

carryVoice: Your line: my master. Whatever You give, good or hard, is what I receive. Until tomorrow.
